speaker: Poet (body-churn)
question: Whom does Māyā plunge?
premises: Māyā, you plunge knowing-and-unknowing folk who know not your greatness.
inference: The body catalogued as delusion's house; knowing and unknowing alike plunged for not knowing her greatness.

speaker: Poet (set-up gods)
question: What of set-up gods?
premises: Gods set up in metal-drawn images — seeing them, 'hā hā alas' say the unfulfilled.
For body-dwellers proud with body-I-ness — what delusion does Māyā not birth.
inference: Installed images leave seers unfulfilled: body-I-ness breeds every delusion.

speaker: Poet (protection)
question: What protects from falling?
premises: From delusion-play-arisen voided-intellect, body-and-all I-ness-born all.
Protect from falling, supreme goddess, self-awareness-formed through effort.
inference: Protection-begging from the all born of delusion-play: effort-born self-awareness as the guard against falling.

speaker: Poet (wonder)
question: How is power beheld?
premises: Terrible-natured, most terrible, non-terrible; higher-and-lower-called, neither lower nor higher.
Manifold-formed Śiva's power — seeing it, abiding in wonder.
inference: Beholding the manifold power — terrible and not — ends in wonder-abiding, not doctrine.

speaker: Poet (no-insistence)
question: What insistence remains?
premises: Dwelling mid the rays of higher-and-lower.
No insistence of mine on being-nonbeing-being-nonbeing judgments.
inference: Mid-ray dwelling dissolves insistence: no grip on any being-nonbeing judgment.

speaker: Poet (both remembered)
question: What is remembered?
premises: Your unsurpassed form flashes, and the other world-made one, O mother.
Remembering both — to the good, fear-giving, boon-giving, supreme goddess.
inference: Both forms remembered together: unsurpassed and world-made — to the good, fear and boon from one goddess.

speaker: Poet (five acts)
question: What is asked of the five-act lady?
premises: Lady of the five acts, supreme-knowing-formed Pārvatī, be gracious.
Lift the fallen beast-fettered one; soothe the child with cool glances.
inference: Double petition: lift the fallen fettered one; soothe the child — cool glances for heat.

speaker: Poet (seal)
question: Who utters these?
premises: Having bowed to perfected gurus, gods, goddess, then yogins.
By Abhinavagupta these fifteen verses uttered.
inference: Lineage-bow then authorship claim: perfected ones first, then the fifteen verses as Abhinavagupta's uttering.
